Class PowerFunctionsRemote

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.lego.PowerFunctionsRemote
public final class PowerFunctionsRemote extends Object
A LEGO Power Functions infrared remote (8885), which drives the motors, lights and servos plugged into an IR Receiver (8884) set to one of its four channels. It is plain Java on top of the raw pulses of Infrared: see there for the wiring of the IR LED (with a series resistor) on the transmit pin, pointed at the receiver.

Every command is a 16-bit message of 4-bit fields (toggle, escape and channel; output and mode; data; and a checksum) sent as a 38 kHz burst of 6 cycles per bit followed by a pause of 10 cycles for a 0, 21 for a 1 and 39 for the start and stop marks, the way the LEGO Power Functions RC protocol and the common Arduino libraries do. Each command is sent six times so the receiver does not miss it, which takes about 80 ms; a motor keeps its speed until the next command or about a second without one, so repeat the command in a loop to keep it running.

Each receiver has two outputs, OUTPUT_RED and OUTPUT_BLUE, and the receiver's channel switch (1 to 4) must match the channel argument. Sending is blocking. Works on both boards. The pulse timings follow the published protocol and have not been verified on a receiver.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public static void begin(int transmitPin)
      Configures transmitPin for the IR LED.

    • setSpeed

      public static void setSpeed(int channel, int output, int speed)
      Runs output of the receiver on channel at speed, -7..7: positive for one direction, negative for the other, 0 lets it coast. Out-of-range values are clamped.

    • brake

      public static void brake(int channel, int output)
      Actively brakes output, unlike setSpeed(channel, output, 0), which lets it coast.

    • setSpeeds

      public static void setSpeeds(int channel, int redSpeed, int blueSpeed)
      Sets both outputs of the receiver on channel in one message, each -7..7 as in setSpeed(int, int, int). It is a single command, so use it to start two motors together.

    • stop

      public static void stop(int channel)
      Lets both outputs of the receiver on channel coast.
